subject: bdbv-2026

trial_anchor.source: Henao-Restrepo AM et al. Lancet 2017;389:505-18 (10.1016/S0140-6736(16)32621-6), Table 3 primary analysis: 0/2108 vaccinated in immediate rings vs 16/3075 eligible in delayed rings, onset >= 10 d after randomisation; VE 100% (95% CI 68.9-100). inputs.name: ring_protected_share
inputs.source: ASSUMPTION: ring-vaccination timing from a declared Zaire calibration (trial-likelihood weighted), carried to BDBV with three further assumptions: the DRC 2018-19 index-onset-to-ring-vaccination delay (median 7 d, IQR 3-10; WHO/INRB preliminary results, April 2019) stretched 1-2x, each calibration set's Zaire onset-to-transmission gamma (mean = serial interval 15.3 d, WHO Ebola Response Team 2014, 10.1056/NEJMoa1411100, Table 2, minus the set's incubation mean drawn across that table's 9.1 to 11.4 d; sd 3.0) kept, and post-exposure credit from the calibration prior (0 to 0.6, with index share 0 to 0.9 and immune onset 2 to 14 d only partly constrained by the fit). method_inputs.name: ve_zaire
method_inputs.source: Henao-Restrepo AM et al. Lancet 2017;389:505-18 (10.1016/S0140-6736(16)32621-6), Table 3 primary analysis: 0/2108 vaccinated in immediate rings vs 16/3075 eligible in delayed rings, onset >= 10 d after randomisation; VE 100% (95% CI 68.9-100). Zaire ebolavirus only. Posterior uses Jeffreys Beta on the conditional binomial split, without the trial's cluster adjustment.

method_inputs.name: strain_match
method_inputs.source: ASSUMPTION: no human or field estimate of Ervebo protection against BDBV. Macaque lethal-challenge studies are small and mixed (from their abstracts): one rVSV-ZEBOV dose gave 75% survival after BDBV challenge against 25% in controls (Falzarano 2011, 10.1093/infdis/jir350); one dose of a blended rVSV-SUDV/ZEBOV vaccine left 1 of 3 surviving, as in controls, while a heterologous prime-boost protected all (Mire 2013, 10.1371/journal.pntd.0002600). Survival after high-dose challenge is not protection against infection, so S keeps a uniform ignorance prior and results are also reported conditional on fixed values

method_inputs.name: potency
method_inputs.source: ASSUMPTION: share of given doses still potent; SitReps record stock-outs, generator failures, idle cold-chain units, thawed and expired doses (SR114-SR186) but never measure potency of doses given

method_inputs.name: durability
method_inputs.source: ASSUMPTION: protection kept over a 90-day horizon; 79.5% antibody responders at 12 months (PREVAIL I, Kennedy 2017, 10.1056/NEJMoa1614067), binding antibody flat over years 1-5 (Huttner 2023, 10.1016/j.cmi.2023.08.026), 76.8% of DRC health workers seropositive against the Kikwit glycoprotein (38.3% against Mayinga) after more than 3 years (Kahusu 2025, abstract, 10.1016/j.vaccine.2025.127537); no correlate of protection, so waning cannot be quantified

method_inputs.name: onset_days
method_inputs.source: ASSUMPTION: days to protection 3-10. Upper end set by the trial's 0 vaccinee cases with onset >= 10 d (Henao-Restrepo 2017). Lower end: 2.5% responders at week 1 (PREVAIL I, Kennedy 2017), 19/20 seroconverted by day 14 at 20 million PFU (Regules 2017, 10.1056/NEJMoa1414216), macaques 2/3 protected when vaccinated 3 d before challenge (Marzi 2015, 10.1126/science.aab3920)

method_inputs.name: horizon_days
method_inputs.source: ASSUMPTION: protection is counted over the 90 days after vaccination, with exposure spread evenly over that window; this sets the pre-exposure timing share

method_inputs.name: pep_effect
method_inputs.source: ASSUMPTION: no protection against infection acquired before immune onset, for pre-exposure rows. Ring and mixed-timing rows differ: their ring component (ring_protected_share) carries post-exposure credit from the calibration prior, 0 to 0.6; the share without that credit is reported alongside

method_inputs.name: indirect_multiplier
method_inputs.source: ASSUMPTION (scenario only, never in the share of all cases averted): chain-breaking multiplier

method_inputs_unused.note: used only by the uncalibrated ring timing mode, which no group uses; ring and mixed rows use ring_protected_share, which carries its own BDBV incubation

release_inputs_notes: SitRep 190 prints no Nord-Kivu vaccination line; Nord-Kivu uses the latest printed split of vaccinated frontline workers (SitRep 188), as SitRep 189 did.
Tshopo: SitRep 190's 100.1 % has no denominator; 14,968 / 14,960 (the SitRep 186 target) = 100.05 %.

A share of all cases averted is reported only for Nord-Kivu, where the vaccinated are split into frontline workers and contacts. Elsewhere the vaccinated are not split into frontline workers and contacts.

Values taken from earlier SitReps (4,027 and 343 from SitRep 188; 4,326 from SitRep 186; 3,300 from SitReps 186-187; 14,960 and Bas-Uele's 2,379 and 13,202 from SitRep 186) are as printed and checked by hand; they are not in a reviewed promotion record, so the record parity check does not cover them. The 36,070 target is in the reviewed SitRep 158 and 159 records.
Ituri: SitRep 190 prints two zone cumulatives that the reviewed record withholds; the range uses SitRep 186's 4,326 over this edition's roster.

Bas-Uele is not in the SitRep 190 vaccination record; its 2,379 and 13,202 are as printed in SitRep 186 and checked by hand. PPL means frontline workers (personnels de premiere ligne) in most SitReps. It is also expanded as persons deprived of liberty (SitReps 179 and 180, where the same hot-meals line reads personnels de premiere ligne in SitReps 181-183), as a special population (SitRep 183, Nord-Kivu) and as the most exposed populations (SitReps 182-183, Ituri).

methodBasis: Decomposition of trial efficacy into field protection: Zaire trial efficacy x strain match x potency x durability x timing x effective coverage, summed over groups by case share for a direct effect only. Strain match is unidentified, so every result is given conditional on it and under a uniform prior, which summarises the prior and is not a data-driven estimate. Coverage comes from a printed rate, a ratio of values printed in the same release, a ratio of values printed in different releases (an assumption with a range on the denominator), or a labelled assumption (named in each group's inputs, with the SitRep each value comes from); every other input is a sourced value, a derived quantity or a labelled assumption.

limitations: A scenario, not a measured effectiveness: no field or human estimate of protection against Bundibugyo virus exists, and strain match is not identified by any SitRep.
The trial anchor is a Zaire ebolavirus estimate; it is never a Bundibugyo figure.
Indirect (chain-breaking) effects are excluded from the share of cases averted; the indirect row is a labelled scenario only.
Ring-vaccination timing comes from a calibration that fits Zaire data poorly; treat ring and mixed-timing rows as bounds.

No national total is computed. A province is computed only for the groups defined for it, each with a printed or a labelled assumed coverage; other record rows are listed as not computed, and zone-level rows are set aside, never summed into a province.
Situational evidence, not clinical or vaccine advice.
